changes: p2 Aṃśuvarman: role 'official' changed to 'other' (he is consulted, 'sākaṃ sampradhārya tadanumatena', and holds no office in the grant); added 'mahāsāmanta' to his titles; noted that 'mahā[rāj-ā]dhirāja' is an editorial restoration and doubtful
p3 dūtaka: name changed from 'Gomin' to '[…]gomin'. Gomin is the honorific element here, and the personal name is lost
p1: dropped the restored epithet 'licchavikulaketu' from titles (bracketed restoration)
relation p2→p1 changed from under_reign_of to other (consultation)
date: added Regmi's reading 'saṃvat 500 … śukla pakṣe' as a doubtful year and pakṣa

purpose: Edict of Śivadeva, issued after consulting Aṃśuvarman, that makes a village with koṭṭamaryādā (exempt from entry by cāṭa-bhaṭa) over to Dolāśikharasvāmin (Chāṅgu Nārāyaṇa), with its boundaries described
notes: The year is damaged. Only Regmi reads '500' and 'śukla pakṣe', so treat both as doubtful. Aṃśuvarman's title 'mahārājādhirāja' rests on a bracketed restoration; in Śivadeva's edicts he is normally styled mahāsāmanta (the header gives 'Mahārājādhirāja-śrī-Sāmanta'). The dūtaka's personal name is lost: only the element 'gomī' (gomin) survives, and 'dūtaka' itself is restored. Dolāśikharasvāmin is a deity (Chāṅgu Nārāyaṇa, cf. No. 58) and is not listed as a person. The epithets bappapādānuddhyāta and licchavikulaketu in l. 2 are editorial restorations. The boundary places named are Candreśvara, Dakṣiṇeśvara, the Dhelantī river, Tekhuṃdul stream and the Goṭana field. Find-spot: Banepā.
